author: BBC News
description:
Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Spanish cities, after hundreds of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.

Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas. Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption.

Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November. The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant."

As the days get shorter and darker, many people notice a change in their mood and energy levels. But when does a normal winter slump become something more serious?
 
Here, BBC Health Correspondent Dom Hughes takes a deep dive into Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD) - a form of depression linked to seasonal changes, most commonly during autumn and winter.

author: BBC News
description:
Iran's security chief says Tehran will attack any US military bases, including in Europe, if they are used to launch attacks on Iran.

Mohsen Rezaei also vowed that not even a single particle of enriched nuclear material will be allowed to leave his country, as part of any negotiations to end the war.

The US Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, is moved out of his Washington DC home to a military base - with US media reporting it's because of Iran-linked threats to his life.

Meanwhile three men have been charged by the US over what they say are a string of Iran-backed terror plots in Europe and America, including the incident at RAF Fairford.

author: BBC News
description:
We take a look at how climate change, extreme weather and the wars in Ukraine and Iran are pushing South Asia closer to the brink of a food and fuel crisis. 

Speaking at the COP31 summit in Turkey, United Nations chief António Guterres warned that "the climate crisis is outrunning us" and that the world is on "the path to mutually assured destruction". 

Experts have added that the effects of climate change are being exacerbated by a "super" El Niño. Farmers in India and the wider region have struggled with droughts this year, Indonesia faced wildfires and Nepal was hit with deadly flash floods.

Meanwhile, the US and Israel's war with Iran, the reduced traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and the targetting of energy infrastructure across the Gulf by Iran and its allies have raised the price of fuel and limited supplies of fertiliser.

Transport and other public services across Spain have faced serious disruption in the first general strike for 14 years called by the main unions over housing and the high cost of living.
 
Demonstrations have taken place across the country, including in Madrid and Barcelona, where tens of thousands marched.
 
Some of the biggest disruption on Wednesday was seen in the main industrial hubs of Madrid and the north-eastern region of Catalonia where traffic was halted on several main roads.
 
The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices.

Real Madrid footballer Vinícius Júnior has sent a message to one of his biggest fans, a young boy in Sudan who lost both of his legs in a drone strike.

Now, his favourite footballer has invited him to meet him and watch a Real Madrid game.

author: BBC News
description:
In his first interview, parliamentary researcher Chris Cash has spoken to the BBC about being accused of spying for China. 

In 2023 Chris Cash and his friend - Chris Berry - were arrested on suspicion of spying for China, but last year the case was suddenly dropped and the pair were acquitted.

Prosecutors said the case was dropped because the government wouldn’t confirm that China was an ‘enemy’ of the UK. 

Chris Cash has given the BBC thousands of messages he exchanged with Chris Berry  between January 2022 and March 2023, which were at the heart of the prosecution’s case.

BBC Politics Investigations Correspondent Joe Pike analyses the messages and asks Chris Cash how information from inside parliament may have reached the upper echelons of the Chinese Communist Party.

title: I was accused of spying for China | BBC News

author: BBC News
description:
An effort to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging war on Iran without congressional authorisation, has failed on Capitol Hill.
 
A majority of the House of Representatives agreed to refer impeachment articles to a committee - essentially killing the effort introduced by dissident Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky - for now.
 
In his first news briefing from the Pentagon in six months, Hegseth called the impeachment effort a "farce" and "sabotage".
 
The bid to find the cabinet secretary guilty of misconduct and ultimately remove him from office was seen as a long shot as it could have required a number of other Republicans to defy President Donald Trump.
